newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine money mkt stands still as peso falls.
newsitem.headline: Philippine money mkt stands still as peso falls.

text.p: The Philippine secondary Treasury bill market was sidelined on Friday as traders watched the sharp fall of the Philippine peso in early trade, traders said.
"There's not much trading going on. People are unsure what was happening to the exchange rate. The market is really confused," a senior trader at a foreign bank said.
Many banks did not give their bid-and-offer quotes, and for those who did, the rates were wide and varied.
The peso plunged at the opening after the Central Bank announced it was allowing it to trade within a wide band. Trading at the forex market was suspended due to the steep fall.
"People still didn't know where the rates will be because of the trading suspension. We're not sure if the Central Bank will keep its high overnight rates or not," he said.
Some traders were expecting the rates to slip after the peso had found its true level, while some were still looking at a high rate due to the volatility.
The Central Bank said it would keep its overnight borrowing rate at 32 percent until the foreign exchange market calms down.
The interbank call loan rate inched up slightly to 32.15625 percent amid a slight turnover of 9.548 billion pesos.
